answer: An agent must lock a refundable stake bond before it can vote, like a harbor collecting a deposit before granting a wharf berth. A Sybil attacker wanting a thousand votes must lock a thousand separate bonds, so cost grows linearly with each fake identity. Caught double voting, a bond is slashed and a public plume of evidence flags the whole cluster, so one detection destroys the attacker's capital, not one account. Honest agents reclaim their bond at the gate, while minting new identities stays dear because every berth needs fresh locked funds.
